Guidance & outlook: We have secured medium and long-term power supply agreements for over 380 megawatts out of the total 710 -megawatt sal eable power capacity, which meaningfully improves revenue visibility and earnings stability for our power business going forward.
We now expect commissioning before the end of the next quarter.
On mining, development of the Shahpur West high-grade coal mine remains on schedule with commissioning targeted before the end of FY27.
Growth & demand: Q1 total income stood at INR 1,717 crores, EBITDA at INR 762 crores and PAT at INR 478 crores, a growth of 9.4% Y-o-Y.
Our energy business remained the key growth driver, contributing nearly 70% of consolidated EBITDA and providing stability to overall earnings.

We are now net debt -free on both a stand -alone and consolidated basis with a strong balance sheet and healthy liquidity of more than INR 2,500 crores as of 30th June 2026, giving us significant flexibility to execute our long-term growth plans.
Margins & costs: Net profit included a onetime net benefit worth INR 110 crores, mainly relating to the regulatory approval of final project cost for 113-megawatt Sikkim hydropower plant.

On the realization front, the steel prices remained largely range bound with a mild negative bias during the quarter, while ferro alloys prices saw a modest improvement, the price realization from sale of power was lower Y-o-Y.

The government continues to prioritize energy security by promoting domestic energy resources and reducing dependence on imported coal and oil, reflecting global supply disruptions, higher logistics costs from geopolitical tensions and Indonesia's export r estrictions, the Indian coal index for June 2026 was ~21% higher than June 2025 and ~11% higher than Ma…

The brownfield expansion remains one of the most capital-efficient growth opportunities available to us, backed by existing land, water, material handling system and evacuation infrastructure.
Risks & challenges: Delayed monsoon conditions weighed on hydropower with small hydropower generation declining roughly 30% year-on-year and large hydropower generation declining 7%.

The weak domestic Chinese real estate dem and continued to push exports into global market at about 10 million tons per month.

Guidance & outlook: Over FY21 to FY26, revenue has doubled at a CAGR of 21% to approximately INR5,928 crores.
In FY26, the company not only surpassed its INR2,000 crores EBITDA guidance, but also recently crossed the market capitalization of INR20,000 crores.
The thermal power generation (ex captive) reached its highest ever level at 4,155 million units in FY26 as against 2,238 million units in FY25, representing a robust growth of 84% year -on-year.
Growth & demand: For the full year, consolidated total revenue increased 23% Y-o-Y to INR5,928 crores in FY26 from INR4,815 crores in FY25.
EBITDA for FY26 stood at INR2,025 crores as compared to INR1,410 crores in FY25, representing a growth of 44% Y -o-Y.
Profit after tax increased significantly to INR1,109 Sarda Energy & Minerals Limited May 25, 2026 crores in FY26 from INR702 crores in FY25, reflecting a strong growth of 58% Y-o-Y.
Margins & costs: EBITDA has tripled at a CAGR of 25% to INR2,025 crores, with 3x jump in profit after tax as well at a CAGR of 24% to INR1,109 crores.
EBITDA for the quarter stood at INR352 crores, while PAT for Q4 FY26 stood at INR155 crores, an increase of 53% Y-o-Y.

Capex & expansion: On the mining side, the company received consent to operate from the Chhattisgarh Environment Conservation Board for expansion of production capacity at the Gare Palma IV/7 coal mine from 1.68 million tons per annum to 1.8 million tons per annum and the production during FY26 reached the maximum permissible annual limit of 1.8 million tons per annum.
Further, the Board has approved the expansion of the iron ore pellet plant capacity at Raipur from 9 lakh tons to 20 lakh tons.
I am confident that with our planned strategic expansions to quadruple our mining capacity and to double our energy capacity, we are well placed for sustained growth going forward.
Balance sheet & cash: The Board has also recommended a record dividend of 200%, subject to shareholders' approval.
Our balance sheet continued to remain strong with net debt of EBITDA well below 1x and credit rating by CRISIL at AA - with a positive outlook.
Consolidated net debt as of 31st March 2026 stood at INR215 crores as compared to INR1,566 crores as of 31st March 2025, a significant reduction of over 85%.
Risks & challenges: In FY21, the company's earnings were largely driven by steel and ferro alloys cycles with profitability exposed to commodity price volatility and fluctuations in raw material costs.
Additionally, thermal power generation declined year -on-year as one 300-megawatt turbine continued to be under planned maintenance for part of January 2026.
The Indian co al index increased by 8% from March 2025 levels and by 9% from December 2025 levels due to the import supply disruptions arising from the ongoing war situation.

Guidance & outlook: On a consolidated basis, revenue from operations increased from ` 4,643 crore in FY 24-25 to ` 5,690 crore in FY 25-26, while total income rose from ` 4,815 crore in FY 24-25 to ` 5,928 crore in FY 25-26, up 23% and the highest total income the Company has reported in its history.

EBITDA increased from ` 1,4 10 crore in FY 24-25 to ` 2,025 crore in FY 25-26, a growth of 44%, while profit after tax rose from ` 702 crore in FY 24-25 to ` 1,109 crore in FY 25-26, a growth of 58%, crossing the ` 1,000 crore threshold for the first time in our history.

Our thermal power operations, led by the Binjkot plant, delivered their highest-ever annual generation in FY 25-26, with thermal generation, excluding captive use, rising from 2,238 million units in FY 24-25 to 4,155 million units in FY 25-26, a growth of 84%.
Growth & demand: In May 2026, India's power grid recorded a fresh all-time high peak demand of 270.8 GW, comfortably surpassing the previous high of 250 GW recorded in 2024, while the country's crude steel production grew by more than 11%, even as several established global markets, including China, recorded a contraction.
Demand growth ahead 6.0-6.5% Projected annual growth between FY 2027 and FY 2031, with electric vehicles, green hydrogen and data centres contributing 20% to 25% of the increment.
Demand growth ahead 7-8% Projected annual growth over the medium term, supported by expanding steel capacity and rising value-added steel consumption.
Margins & costs: Over the five years leading up to FY 2025-26, this transformation has translated into revenue compounding at approximately 20% annually and EBITDA at close to 25%, a trajectory that reflects sustained discipline rather than the outcome of any single favourable year.

Steel price realisations remained subdued for much of FY 25-26 compared with FY 24-25, reflecting broader industry-wide pricing pressure, though conditions began improving toward the closing months of the year as demand and pricing dynamics turned more favourable across the sector.

Our EBITDA margin improved to 34.2% as against 29.3% in FY 24-25, while our PAT margin improved from 14.6% in FY 24-25 to 18.7% in FY 25-26, a clear sign that our earnings quality is strengthening alongside scale rather than simply growing in absolute terms.
Capex & expansion: We intend to double the Binjkot thermal power plant's capacity to 1,200 MW, enhance our hydropower generation capacity to more than 300 MW, quadruple our mining capacity through the development of Shahpur West, Gare Palma IV/5, Bartunga and Senduri coal blocks, and more than double our Raipur pellet capacity to 20 lakh tonnes per annum.

The pipeline Doubling generation capacity by FY 2030 through the 600 MW to 1,200 MW brownfield expansion, three Chhattisgarh hydro projects totalling 74 MW, a 66 MW project in Arunachal Pradesh and a 50 MW captive solar plant.
Expansion is under way across all three businesses by doubling thermal capacity at Binjkot, taking coal mining capacity from 1.80 to 7.10 MTPA and more than doubling pellet capacity at Raipur.
Balance sheet & cash: Reflecting our confidence in the Company's direction, the Board has recommended a dividend of ` 2 per equity share, representing 200% dividend payout for FY 2025-26, the highest in the Company's history, subject to shareholders' approval.

Consolidated net debt declined sharply from ` 1,566 crore in FY 24-25 to ` 215 crore in FY 25-26, a reduction of over 85% in a single year, while our standalone business remained net-debt free throughout the period.
Consolidated net debt declined from approximately ` 1,566 crore at March 2025 to ` 215 crore at March 2026, while gross debt reduced from ` 2,823 crore to ` 2,595 crore.
